The expected busiest link carries about 1.34 times the mean load.

**Mechanism:** Each of the 128 leaf-switch/link sets receives a Binomial(448, 1/8) load. This has mean 56 and standard deviation sqrt(448·(1/8)·(7/8)) = 7. Treating the 128 loads as nearly independent (they are weakly negatively correlated within a leaf), the finish time is set by the maximum of 128 such draws.

**Estimate:** For 128 draws the expected normal maximum is about 2.6σ above the mean. The binomial's slight positive skew (about 0.11) fattens the upper tail. I computed tail probabilities P(max ≥ k) with an Edgeworth-corrected tail and summed them to get E[max] ≈ 74.8. This is an analytic estimate, not a Monte Carlo run.

The ratio is therefore 74.8 / 56 ≈ 1.34. Even with perfectly uniform random hashing, the busiest link carries about 34% more than the mean.
